title: How can we make a rectangle with twice the area of a triangle?
description: A triangle needs a rectangle of twice its area. One method builds the rectangle on the same base and height, and another joins two copies into a parallelogram, then cuts and slides it into a rectangle.
teaching_notes: One idea: a rectangle on the same base and height has twice the area of the triangle. Watch for students who forget the half in the area of a triangle.

video_script.why: The child uses cut and slide from the solved example, and the area of a triangle, to build a rectangle of twice the area in two ways.
video_script.substitution: Build the rectangle on the base and height, or join two copies and cut and slide.
video_script.anchor: the book's triangle ABC with its base BC and height AD
video_script.payoff_line: Build a rectangle on the base and height, or join two copies and cut and slide

final_answer.value: build the rectangle on the base and height, or join two copies of the triangle into a parallelogram, then cut and slide
final_answer.spoken: build a rectangle on the base and height, or join two copies and cut and slide

hold_back: Build a rectangle on the base
maths_rules: triangle ABC with base BC and height AD; area = 1/2 × BC × AD
method 1: the line through A parallel to BC and the perpendiculars at B and C make rectangle BCFE with BE = AD, area = BC × AD = 2 × triangle
method 2: a half turn of a copy about the midpoint of AC gives the parallelogram ABCA' with base BC and height AD, area = 2 × triangle; cut and slide gives a rectangle BC by AD
both methods give a rectangle of area BC × AD = twice the triangle
video_script.design: One triangle all video, two methods, one rectangle of twice its area.
